newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EA-Generali '96 premiums, net profit up.
newsitem.headline: EA-Generali '96 premiums, net profit up.

text.p: Insurer EA-Generali said on Thursday 1996 group premium income rose to 42.7 billion schillings, from 36.88 billion a year earlier, as its life insurance business boomed.

In a statement, EA-Generali said net profit for the year rose to 600 million schillings, from 479.6 million in 1996. The Italian-controlled group said it expected to pay an unchanged dividend of 17 schillings per share.

The group warned that premium income was likely to remain flat in the current year. "The year 1997 is marked by a further increase in competition, which will result in a stagnation of premium incomes," it said.

In Austria alone, premium income rose almost 20 percent to 28.7 billion schillings. The increase was powered by a 61 percent increase in life insurance premiums as Austrians scrambled to buy policies ahead of a tax change in May 1996.
In Germany, EA-Generali reported a 4.6 percent rise in premiums to 11.2 billion schillings. In Hungary, premiums increased almost 22 percent to 1.8 billion schillings.
EA-Generali is majority-owned by Italy's Assecurazioni Generali SpA.
